segment.description: Beech Lake (USGS/TVA 'Beech Reservoir') on the Beech River at Lexington, Henderson County, West Tennessee. TWRA Region 1 winter put-and-take trout lake (catalog: seasonMonths Nov-Mar) over a warmwater bass/bream/catfish fishery; one of the 'Beech River Watershed Lakes' group in TWRA's regulation exceptions.
segment.boundaries: Entire lake. TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule lists 'Beech Lake' as a Winter-type Rainbow Trout site (repo workbook rows: Henderson Co., 1/14/2026 and TBD 12/2026; the schedule page renders dates 1/13/2026 and 2/10/2026 adjacent to the Beech Lake entry). No trout stockings of any other type found for the lake.

coldSource.notes: Dam identity basis: USGS inactive station 03594413 is named 'BEECH LAKE NEAR LEXINGTON, TENN (TVA)' (Henderson Co., HUC 06040001 Lower Tennessee-Beech, 35.66118,-88.41727). TVA's 'Beech Reservoir' page (tva.com, verified via WebSearch snippet only — tva.com blocks plain fetch) describes flood-storage of 4,430 acre-feet, ~3.65 miles long, and Beech Dam as a non-hydro dam; a WebSearch synthesis adds the dam was built early 1960s for water supply/flood control/recreation. No cold-release (deep-draw) regime documented; no evidence the lake receives or needs cold dam water.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover evidence found. Program design is winter put-and-take: the only trout rows for Beech Lake in TWRA's 2026 schedule are Winter-type, and the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 states hatchery-supported streams and lakes 'are primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'. Warmwater stockings (bluegill/redear) also appear for the lake in TWRA's warmwater stocking archive.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented. The Trout Management Plan states wild trout are generally limited to East Tennessee's mountain streams; no wild-trout listing or record exists for this West Tennessee reservoir.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Winter put-and-take only: TWRA's 2026 schedule carries Beech Lake (Henderson Co.) solely as a Winter rainbow site, and the Trout Management Plan states hatchery-supported lakes like this are warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round.
